inventory.anchor: class RecursiveMakeBackend, the objs_ref assignment near line 1607 (enclosing def name not extracted)
evidence: -        objs_ref = " \\\n    ".join(os.path.relpath(o, obj.objdir) for o in objs)
inventory.notes: Applies to every platform and every build, not only Win32: relative object paths are replaced by absolute ones unconditionally. The comment blames mozmake 4.4.1 on Win32 for paths over about 150 chars; that claim is the author's and was not checked here. Could be a helper call in our own file, but a one-line change is already small.

verifier.why: mozmake 4.4.1 path-length workaround is a build-system change not tied to a Firefox version, so build, same as the other win-long-build-paths files.

inventory.anchor: _downloadPayload (def at line 634), plus import signal at the top of the file
inventory.notes: Per-file SIGALRM watchdog for slow downloads in the cross-compile build. The comment ties it to a flaky CDN, not to a Firefox version, so it is build and not port-fix. On native Windows, SIGALRM does not exist and the watchdog is skipped; the comment says main() sets a socket default timeout instead. Process-wide signal handler: not safe in threaded use. Move the watchdog into an own helper and keep one call line here.

verifier.why: Checked against the diff and tree; no correction needed.
